A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SciRIFF and contain readable main text, figures, tables and appendices. The retained task taxonomy, evaluation appendix and earlier science analyses provide clear correspondence despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v3 reports original finetuning experiments, scientific and general-task evaluations, and checkpoint, data-mixture and training-size ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments across several model families and training configurations, new template ablations, and retained continual-finetuning analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use expert-written instruction templates and supervised finetuning on SciRIFF, optionally mixed with general instructions. The earlier base-model and continual-finetuning procedures remain in v4 Section 4.3. New backbones and template comparisons extend the experiments; no new proposed algorithm, objective or inference component is established.

E1.justification: The 54-task science resource and nine scientific evaluation tasks remain. However, v4 removes evaluations on MMLU, GSM8K, Big Bench Hard, CodexEval, AlpacaEval and TruthfulQA, including their appendix results, substantially narrowing evaluated capabilities. The new template variants reuse existing scientific tasks.

E2.justification: v4 replaces the earlier GPT-3.5/GPT-4 comparisons with six frontier comparators, including GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-4o. Table 2 also adds SciLitLLM, BioMedical-Llama3, BioMistral and CodeLlama. Simple and GPT-4o-generated templates become evaluated alternatives. Earlier Llama 2/Tulu continual-finetuning comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New principal experiments use Qwen 2.5-1.5B, Llama 3.2-3B and Llama 3.1-8B configurations with 70.5K science training instances. Reported training changes from two to five epochs, and the declared LLM judge changes from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o. Template ablations introduce matching evaluation prompts. Retained task-level appendix descriptions still name GPT-3.5, leaving judge documentation inconsistent; legacy-result reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B add expert-versus-simple-versus-generated template ablations on two backbones. They investigate output-format failures on Qasper and SciERC and report an analysis excluding those tasks. Earlier science checkpoint and training-size analyses remain, while general-capability ablation outcomes are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its own model experiments. Both present point estimates and aggregate scores.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive backbone, baseline and template results; for example, Table 2 reports 62.8 for Llama 3.1-8B trained on SciRIFF versus 40.0 with Tulu alone. It removes general-task scores and detailed older 7B/70B ablation results, while retaining their science averages and Figure 3. New scores do not establish same-setting improvements over v3 because models and evaluation conditions differ.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, propositions or proofs. Retained empirical metric descriptions and training-size notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds sample-efficient SciTulu adaptation, 28.1%/6.5% scientific gains and preservation of general capabilities. v4 foregrounds the expert-written resource and evaluation suite, claims 70.6% average gains across newer models, and adds template-superiority claims. General-capability preservation disappears from the main contribution claims; efficient adaptation becomes a subsidiary analysis.

C2.justification: v3 emphasizes model-scale differences, negative task transfer and preventing forgetting. v4 develops interpretations of base-versus-instruct data mixing, grounded attribution versus general reasoning, and generated-template format failures. It adds substantive limitations concerning chat-style interactions, the largest models and bias in peer-review-derived data.

D1.justification: v4 adds source-dataset citations, licenses and links in Table 6, documents manual conversion scripts for 50 tasks, and supplies template-generation instructions and reusable templates in Appendices B and F. It newly states the 4.1K evaluation size and approximately 40 H100 GPU-hours per 7B training run; v3 instead identified TPU v3-128 hardware.

R1.justification: v4 adds extensive source-dataset references and substantive positioning relative to SciLitLLM, SciASSESS, SciArena and SciReas. It expands the distinction between grounded literature understanding, abstract reasoning and synthetic instruction resources, while dropping several earlier negative-transfer and general-training references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset explanation, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Earlier ablations become separate continual-finetuning and scaling sections, instruction-mix statistics move to Appendix A, and template, limitations, ethics and author-contribution sections expand the document structure.

P2.justification: The main document changes from one-column to two-column layout. Results tables are substantially reorganized, older detailed-result tables disappear, and provenance and template-ablation tables plus boxed Figures 6–13 are added. Figures 1–5 retain their substantive content with resizing, relocation and caption edits.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens support for SciRIFF through controlled experiments across additional backbones, specialist comparisons and direct template tests. Its provenance table and reusable templates improve auditability. These benefits are offset partly by removing general-capability evaluations and detailed older results, and by inconsistent GPT-4o/GPT-3.5 judge descriptions in Appendix D. The evidence supports a net improvement, but these losses and documentation problems limit its overall significance.
